newsitem.title: USA: Raleigh, N.C., approves arena financing plan.
newsitem.headline: Raleigh, N.C., approves arena financing plan.

text.p: Raleigh City Council has approved a revised plan to use hotel taxes for the final $48 million needed to build a $120 million sports arena.
After months of negotiations with Wake County, the city council approved the measure in a 5-3 vote Tuesay.

If the county commission approves, the plan would give the Centennial Authority $48 million of revenues from the countywide six percent hotel tax. The authority would have the option of repaying the debt in 10 years rather than the previously agreed 19 years.

The proposal would give the city increased representation on the authority and would require that $2 million of hotel tax revenues be used for other tourism and entertainment projects. It would also require that the tax-exempt arena pay the city and county about $1.5 million annually in lieu of property taxes.

The Centennial Authority already has $72 million committed to the arena. That includes $22 million previously earmarked from hotel taxes plus state funds and money raised by North Carolina State University boosters.
The 21,000-seat arena would house the university's basketball team and possibly a professional hockey team.
The authority could either issue revenue bonds for construction or draw on a line of credit backed by the hotel tax.
